content.text:
`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes all 7 tests. I fixed two bugs in `household/bills.py` and changed one test expectation that was wrong.

**Code fixes in `household/bills.py`:**
1. **`split_bill` lost leftover cents.** It gave everyone `total // people` and dropped the remainder, so 1001 split two ways came out as `[500, 500]`. It now uses `divmod` and gives the leftover cents one each to the first people, as the docstring says. 1001 split two ways is now `[501, 500]`.
2. **`due_dates` crashed after December.** It added to the month number without carrying into the next year, so it asked for "month 13" and errored. It now rolls over to January of the next year. Clamping to the last day of short months still works.

**Test change in `tests/test_bills.py`:** `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3)` to return `[333, 333, 333]`. That adds up to 999, not 1000, so it contradicts the docstring and the remainder test next to it. It only passed because of the bug. I changed the expected value to `[334, 333, 333]`. If you meant to drop the extra cent, tell me and I'll change the code and the remainder test instead.

I haven't committed anything.
